projects.title: Migration of 24-bit DSP code base to a new 32-bit architecture for Kalimba DSP
projects.description:

• Developed test scripts in MATLAB to validate DSP code revisions using FIO interface
• Analysed test results and compiled test database for various audio DSP modules

projects.title: Enhanced Voice Capture for Mobile Devices Using a Mixed-Response-Type Array
projects.description: NSF SBIR (Phase I) to develop very small audio subsystems for mobile audio devices with unprecedented noise and interference reduction. Audio subsystems are fundamental to many high-volume portable devices such as mobile phones, media tablets, and digital voice recorders. Multiple microphones can enhance audio capture and improve signal quality by reducing acoustic noise interference, but traditional arrays of separated omni-directional microphones require large spacing (aperture) between microphones to achieve high discrimination. The small size of mobile communication devices thus fundamentally degrades the performance of existing array technologies. Researchers have developed practical "zero-aperture" mixed-response-type arrays that retain high directional selectivity with very closely spaced microphones, and innovative signal-processing methods that achieved unprecedented background noise and interference reduction with high target signal quality using such arrays in other applications, most notably in real-time voice tracking and steering-vector estimation and their seamless integration with adaptive beam-forming. Successful research could fundamentally improve the signal capture and noise rejection of small mobile electronic voice communication devices, thus greatly improving their most fundamental function and enabling their effective use in a wider range of environments.
